I've been through the books and
         things don't add up. I didn't make
         nearly what it says I did.

I did what was right all along.
         You think living here was a free
         ride? Don't you dare question me.
Just then, ON TV the climax of the match happens. They stop
talking and watch on as KERRY beats MR PERFECT. The BOYS
and FRITZ jump up and celebrate. But KEVIN is seething.
FRITZ turns back to him.

Atta boy Kerry. That's how you do
         it. Look at your uncle boys.

KEVIN doesn't respond. But he knows what he will do.

The Ranch at last light on a chilly winter night. The glow
of Christmas inside. KEVIN and PAM are there with DORIS and
FRITZ. KERRY arrives home for Christmas to A HERO RETURNS.

Hey! Welcome home champ. We've
         been watching every match on the

Thanks Pop. Guys, this is Tania.

TANIA, KERRY'S new girlfriend, is with him. They are both
drunk and maybe high. TANIA is overly aggressive in hugging
each member of the family.
It's so nice to meet you all.

Let me get a look at you. You look
         strong son. WWF Intercontinental
         Champion, second biggest title in
         wrestling now that your brother
         ruined our promotion. I knew it
         was time to retire when I did.

KEVIN and PAM share a glance in disbelief at FRITZ's rant.

Kerry can you get me a drink
         honey.

KERRY goes to the Kitchen to grab beer from the fridge.

Oh, Dad, Dad, I got something for
         you for Christmas, but I can't
         wait. I really want to give it to
         you now. Is that OK?

Kerry, wait till Christmas
         morning. Don't be silly.

KERRY comes back in and gives a beer to TANIA and drinks
another. Now everyone realizes he's drunk. FRITZ is upset.

It's just so good. And Tania and I
         are going to Mexico for Christmas.

I thought you were home for
         Christmas.

I am, this is Christmas. We just
         got a great deal for a Christmas
         day flight to Mexico and we need
         some rest. I've been hitting it
         hard out there, you know.

KERRY digs through his bag and pulls out a GIFT.

Please take it now, Dad. Please.

KERRY is so eager, like a child looking for approval. FRITZ
reluctantly unwraps it. It is a beautiful REVOLVER.

It's a Smith and Wesson .357 50th
         anniversary! What do you think?

It's great son, thank you.

FRITZ puts the gun in the living room GUN CASE.
Don't do that. Let's shoot it now.
I don't want to shoot it now.

You always shoot a gun when you
         get it.
I don't want to shoot it, Kerry.
Kerry! What is wrong with you?

Watch it son. You've brought
         company to the house, and we don't
         want to be rude. Just settle down,
         and we can have a nice dinner that
         your mother worked hard to
         prepare.

Now come tell me, when are you
         getting your world title shot over
         there? I see your old tag team
         partner Hellwig's holding, that
         guy's got nothing on you, never
         has.

Soon Pop, soon.

KERRY goes to the kitchen to grab another beer. KEVIN
follows.

Hey! Sorry brother, I'm excited to
         be home.
They hug. A CHRISTMAS ALBUM plays from the living room.

You too.

KEVIN looks at him hard, there is something missing behind
KERRY'S eyes.

Stop it.

KERRY cracks three beers and hands one to KEVIN. They
cheers and sip.

THE PHONE RINGS. KEVIN wakes and picks up before it can
wake the house.

Oh good, I wasn't sure you'd be
            up.

I'm up, I'm up. What's going on
            Ker? Where are you?
KERRY sits on the edge of the bed. He's drunk, high.
I'm back in Dallas. In a hotel.

Hey, why didn't you tell us you
         lost the belt. We could of been
         there for you.

I don't know. Didn't think about
         it.

KEVIN just shakes his head. KERRY starts to cry.

I'm scared man. I'm out of
         control.
You've got to get some help.

I'm in pain man, I'm in pain all
         the time. I'm fucking deformed. It
         takes so much to hide it -
It doesn't show in the ring.

I'm not getting a new contract.
         They're sticking me in house shows
         from now on. They don't want me
         anymore. I've got nowhere to go.
         I've got no one.

That wasn't anything.

KEVIN doesn't know what to say.
I need someone, I need family.

I can't. Your boys can't see me
         like this.

Let's go get some breakfast or
         something. Or meet me at home. Mom
         can cook us up some pancakes.
I just want it all to end.
No you don't. You don't mean that.

I do. I'm alone. All alone.

KEVIN is losing patience.

I'm a piece of shit. I'm fucking
         cursed. I want to die.

How are you going to say that to
         me, after everything?

It's in me. It's taken over.

This hits a nerve. Outside the sun rises. KEVIN digs deep -
calms down.

Kerry, just tell me where you are
         and I'll come get you.

KERRY hangs up. KEVIN thinks for a moment, then calls home.

Dad, Dad. Sorry for the early
         call.

It's OK. I'm heading out to do
         some work.

Look, I just spoke to Kerry. He's
         in a pretty bad state. I'm worried
         about him. I'm going to come out
         there. We need to figure out how
         to help him -

I'm working Kevin. I don't have
         time for this. You boys need to
         work it out between yourselves.

Just look out for him Dad. I'll be
         out there as soon as I can.

FRITZ hangs up.

elements.name: b
elements.content: INT. KEVIN'S TRUCK / EXT. THE VON ERICH RANCH - MORNING

KEVIN drives out to the ranch. He sees his father working
in the field. He looks towards the house and sees a rental
car parked strangely on the front lawn. The front door to
the house is wide open. KEVIN gets out of his truck and
walks up to the rental car. Nothing inside. He walks
towards the house, steps onto the porch, and is about to
enter through the door when a GUN SHOT GOES OFF. HE
freezes. Looks around. He starts to search when he sees
KERRY, laying limp under the tree they called CHUCK HOWLEY.

KEVIN runs to his brother and finds him laying limp, a
bloody mess, gun shot through the chest. The gun he got his
father for Christmas is the weapon.

KEVIN turns to see FRITZ lumbering across the field towards
them. KEVIN is overcome by rage. He rushes FRITZ and
tackles him knocking him flat on his back. FATHER AND SON

I told you to stop him, to look
         out for him. You didn't take care
         of him, you didn't take care of
         any of them.

FRITZ, still strong as an OX, rolls KEVIN over.

He called you and you didn't help
         him. You killed Kerry, you took my
         favorite son from me.

You were here, you could have
         stopped him.

You coward, blaming me. Always
         blaming me, never looking at
         yourself. If you were brave like
         your brothers, you'd kill yourself
         too.

KEVIN, with a surge of rage overturns the giant FRITZ VON
ERICH and slams him down. KEVIN strangles FRITZ for a long
moment, seeming like he won't ever let go. FRITZ struggles
to breathe and submits. Just as FRITZ is about to run out
of air, KEVIN let's go. FRITZ lays still, breathing heavy.
Defeated.

KEVIN picks up KERRY and walks away. FRITZ sits up and
stares at the blood and the gun on the grass.

elements.name: b
elements.content: INT. THE VON ERICH RANCH - DINING ROOM - MOMENTS LATER

elements.name: b
elements.content: KERRY'S SUICIDE NOTE IS IN PLACE OF THE GUN:

I don't know what is on the other side, but I can't be here
anymore. Tonight I walk with my brothers.

KEVIN puts KERRY'S BODY on the dining room table. KEVIN
looks down at another lost brother. He kisses his mouth.

elements.name: b
elements.content: EXT. THE VON ERICH RANCH - MAGIC HOUR

THE CAMERA floats through the field as KERRY'S SOUL walks.
He looks down and sees his foot is back. He jumps up and
down on it, happy.

KERRY sits in a small boat drifting across the water. A
FIREFLY guides him. He turns a corner revealing a DOCK, the
same dock where they swam as kids. MIKE and DAVID sit,
waiting for him.

KERRY steps out of the boat and onto the dock. They hug and
kiss each other on the cheeks. Each hug is tender, physical
and loving and gentle, unlike anything in their life.
MIKE is healthy with long hair wearing a pink bandana,
guitar strapped over his back. He looks like a 70s rock
star.

Mikey.

DAVID towers even taller, looking his best, a strapping
cowboy. He wears a massive GOLD CHAMPIONSHIP BELT.

World Champion of the afterlife.
         Dad said you would be.

Where's Jack Jr?

The BROTHERS gesture towards the FIREFLY. The firefly
disappears and then KERRY feels a tap on his back. He turns
to look down at a sweet scruffy little boy, around 6. This
is JACK JR.

I guess you're my oldest brother
         Jackie.

KERRY picks him up. He is pure and gentle sweetness.

Good to meet you.

The FOUR brothers huddle together. Reunited.

KEVIN sits at the table, alone, holding KERRY's hand,
looking out the window, comforted by the thought of them
all being together.

The Sportatorium is completely empty. KEVIN signs over the
business to a wrestling promoter, JERRY.

Thanks Kevin. I'd love for you to
         stay on wrestling if you want.

I appreciate it. I could use the
         extra work.

Hey, just so you know, your daddy
         called me out to the ranch. Tried
         to intimidate me out of buying
         this from you.

KEVIN just laughs. Shakes his head.

He never stops. Glad it didn't
         work.

They look around the building.

I'm not going to be using the
         Sportatorium so you might want to
         get out of your lease. Though I
         don't know what else they can use
         this place for.

Yeah.

JERRY steps away. KEVIN takes one last look at the empty
arena.

THE HOUSE FEELS COLD, DARK, EMPTY. FRITZ arrives home from
a day of working in the fields. The lights are off, the
house feels different.

I'm in here.

He walks through to the kitchen to find her painting. He has
never seen this in their 45 years together.

I didn't make anything. I'm not
         hungry.

FRITZ sits down across from her. The couple sit together in
silence.

A NEW DAY...KEVIN and PAM lay in bed entwined. PAM is
heavily pregnant. Dogs and cats all around. All love. KEVIN
whispers to her belly, trying not to wake the kids.

The BOYS burst into the room and jump on their parents.

Good morning.

KEVIN scoops them up into a power slam. The boys play
wrestle on the bed.

A beautiful afternoon in the back yard. KEVIN watches his
SONS play football like the uncles they didn't get to know.
It fills him with joy but also breaks his heart. He is
boiling over with emotion and finally, for the first time,
KEVIN begins to cry. His BOYS notice. They stop playing and
walk over to him, confused.

I'm sorry. I'm sorry boys, you
         shouldn't see this. A man doesn't
         cry, I'm sorry.

It's OK dad, really it's OK. You
         can cry. Everyone cries.

Yeah, what are you talking about,
         we cry all the time.

The BOYS get on either side of him and hug him. He sobs *
harder, letting it all out. The BOYS are naturally *
affectionate and don't hesitate to show him warmth.
Why do you think you're sad?

I guess cause I used to be a
         brother, and now I'm not a brother
         anymore.

Oh. Well, we'll be your brothers,
         Dad.

Yeah, we'll be your brothers Dad.

The BOYS and KEVIN hug. He holds them tight.

Thanks boys. Thank you.

KEVIN gives them each a kiss on the cheek. He looks at
them. He feels love and feels loved. Something lifts. KEVIN
and the BOYS get up and start playing football together.
The camera rises up. PAM walks out into the grass with the
dogs to join them. The camera keeps rising to reveal the
beautiful land where they now live. It is humble and
idyllic, full of warmth, love, and possibility. The camera
continues to rise up and up and up.

In 2009 The Von Erich Family was inducted into the WWE Hall
of Fame.

To this day they are considered one of the greatest
families in the history of wrestling.



Kevin and Pan have been married for over 40 years.

They bought a ranch and everyone came to live with them.

All four children and thirteen grandchildren.
